newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee gains mildly as dollar buyers abstain.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee gains mildly as dollar buyers abstain.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.862/872 against the dollar on Wednesday, up from the day's opening level of 35.87/88, dealers said.
Two of Tuesday's major dollar buyers -- the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and a Calcutta-based state-run bank -- were not active on Wednesday, leading to the rupee's recovery, they said.
"It was quiet today and the market was one-sided with only dollar sellers," said the chief forex dealer at a foreign bank.
On Tuesday, the RBI had bought dollars at 35.87 a dollar, its highest purchase price in recent months.
The forward dollar premia saw some fluctuation following statements attributed to the RBI governor, a dealer said.
The six-month annualised premium closed at 7.47 percent compared to the previous close of 7.58 percent, dealers said.
On Monday, the chief of term-lending bank Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) said he did not see long-term interest rates falling significantly.

"I endorse what the RBI chief said recently - that long-term interest rates are unlikely to fall as long as inflation is on the rise and the government's borrowing programme continues," IDBI chairman S.H. Khan had told a news conference.
